@graph.name: Curves and Transfers
@graph.description: Conveyor curves and transfers are the directional handling modules that change the path or orientation of a case without manual handling: 90° transfers, curves, turntables and pop-up transfers. TRF Industrial Automation engineers them as part of the TRFIntraflow platform, together with the straight runs, buffers, routing and controls around them.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a 90° Transfer and a Curve?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curve carries the case around a bend while it stays on the same conveyor. A 90° transfer moves the case from one conveyor onto another at a right angle. Curves give continuity, with no transfer point to manage, while transfers make it possible to join, split or feed lines. TRF chooses between them based on the unit, the layout and the spacing needed.

mainEntity.name: Which Industries Use Conveyor Curves and Transfers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any plant that moves packed cases, cartons, trays or totes toward a palletizer or a warehouse, especially where several packaging areas share one palletizing zone. That includes food processing, beverage, consumer packaged goods, protein processing, frozen food, pet food and personal care manufacturers.
